reference: GNU coreutils link, executed by system Bash with /usr/bin:/bin on PATH. The runner compares exit status, stdout, and the complete fixture tree, including file bytes and hard-link identity.
coverage: Hard-link creation with ordinary and whitespace-containing relative paths
The -- option terminator for dash-prefixed operands
Existing-destination, missing-target, and directory-target failures and their file effects
Wrong-operand-count status compared with GNU coreutils
Deferred ownership and cross-filesystem permission boundaries
exclusions: Cross-owner and cross-filesystem hard-link behavior are deferred because they need distinct UIDs, controlled protected-hardlink policy, or separate filesystems in a disposable VM.
The command only creates hard links; symlink operations belong to the separate ln loadable and are outside this suite.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash reports link as a builtin and exposes the short description documented by the loadable source.
cases.stdout:
builtin
link - POSIX link — create a hard link.

cases.purpose: Create a hard link from an existing file and compare bytes and shared inode identity with GNU coreutils.
cases.script: printf payload > target; link target alias

cases.purpose: Create a hard link between nested relative paths whose components contain spaces.
cases.script: mkdir 'source dir' 'destination dir'; printf payload > 'source dir/file name'; link 'source dir/file name' 'destination dir/alias name'

cases.purpose: Verify -- ends option processing so both dash-prefixed path operands are treated as filenames.
A failed hard-link attempt must leave an existing destination and its contents unchanged.
cases.script: printf source > source; printf keep > destination; set +e; link source destination; rc=$?; set -e; [[ $rc -eq 1 ]]; printf 'rejected=%s\n' "$rc"

cases.purpose: A missing target must fail and must not create the requested link name.
cases.script: set +e; link missing destination; rc=$?; set -e; [[ $rc -eq 1 ]]; [[ ! -e destination && ! -L destination ]]; printf 'rejected=%s\n' "$rc"

cases.purpose: A directory cannot be hard-linked; verify failure and absence of a destination entry.
cases.script: mkdir source-dir; set +e; link source-dir destination; rc=$?; set -e; [[ $rc -eq 1 ]]; [[ ! -e destination && ! -L destination ]]; printf 'rejected=%s\n' "$rc"

cases.purpose: Compare the status and diagnostic policy for an invalid one-operand invocation against GNU coreutils.
Exercise hard-link permission checks across an ownership boundary.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM or reviewed privilege-separated mock that can create two distinct UIDs, arrange a sticky writable directory containing a differently owned source, and set the protected-hardlinks policy. The provided fixtures use one unprivileged identity; do not alter host users, ownership, or kernel policy.

cases.purpose: Verify a hard-link attempt across filesystems fails without creating the destination.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM with two private writable filesystems mounted at fixture directories, or a reviewed syscall mock that returns EXDEV for link(). Mount operations are outside this run; both reference and candidate must see the same isolated filesystem boundary.
